lifecycles._note: KMS transit-key CRYPTO lifecycle (Wave 2 coverage). The existing 'security-kms-key' lifecycle covers create/get/list/update-description/delete; this sibling covers the 9 remaining transit WRITE ops + the 1 managed-kms WRITE. Spine: create transit key (key_type 'advanced', purpose 'rsa-2048' from data/api_bodies.json security/kms/createkey) -> capture $.key.id (confirmed envelope) -> exercise crypto + rotation writes -> delete (schedule deletion). All crypto/rotation steps are optional+grouped so an unexpected 4xx (e.g. a purpose/key_type that does not support a given op, or asymmetric-vs-symmetric mismatch) isolates as a warning and still RECORDS coverage for that endpoint. Bodies from data/api_bodies.json (datakey/encryptdata/hmac/signdata/verifydata/rotatekey/changerotateinfo/changestatekey) + data/api_docs.json schemas; _UNPROVEN provenance (no live 2xx yet). NOTE on purpose: an rsa-2048 (asymmetric) key supports sign/verify/encrypt/decrypt but NOT hmac/datakey (which need a symmetric key); each such op is isolated optional so it records its endpoint then warns. encrypt returns a 'vault:v..' ciphertext used (best-effort soft-capture) to feed decrypt/rewrap; when the soft-capture is absent the doc-sample ciphertext from api_bodies is sent (still records the endpoint, expects 4xx). sign returns a signature fed to verify likewise. managed-kms keys are SYSTEM-managed and cannot be created by the OpenAPI -> update-managed-key-description targets a {unique} id (a seeded placeholder, never a real managed key) so it records the PUT /v1/managed-kms/transit/* write endpoint and 4xx's, isolated optional. (Earlier this used {managed_key_id}, an uncaptured placeholder that the validator now rejects as undefined; {unique} normalizes to '*' for catalog matching identically while resolving cleanly.)

Light, READ-ONLY (no writes, no cleanup). Closes the static id-bound GET gap GET /v1/managed-kms/transit/{key_id} (showmanagedkey) by the list->soft-capture->show idiom (the same pattern iam-readonly-shows uses). managed-kms keys are SYSTEM-managed: there is NO create in the OpenAPI, so a synthetic id would be a guaranteed-404 dead read — instead we list the caller's managed keys (listmanagedkeys, GET /v1/managed-kms/transit, ManagedKeyPageResponse) and soft-capture a REAL key_id from the first item ($.keys[0].id), then show it. A bare account may have system-managed keys (real 2xx) or none (the segment stays a {placeholder} -> normalizes to the catalog '*' key so the GET is still CALLED and the endpoint statically reachable, 4xx-ing harmlessly). Both steps optional with tolerant [200,400,403,404]. Envelope grounded in data/api_docs.json: ManagedKeyPageResponse.keys[] -> ManagedKey.id (response_example $.keys[].id); the show returns ManagedKeyShowResponse{key:ManagedKey}. Does NOT touch the non-managed /v1/kms/transit create/delete (those live in security-kms-key + the crypto lifecycle above).

steps.name: list-managed-keys
steps._note: listmanagedkeys (zero required params; size/page/sort/name all optional). Soft-captures a REAL managed key_id from the first list item (ManagedKeyPageResponse.keys[].id). Drives show-managed-key below. Tolerant [200,400,403,404]: a bare account may have no managed keys (empty list) or be denied (403) — either way the show is still CALLED.

steps.name: show-managed-key
steps._note: id-bound read (showmanagedkey). Closes GAP-get-id for GET /v1/managed-kms/transit/{key_id}. Keys off the list-captured managed_key_id (a real id when the account has system-managed keys -> 2xx); if none, the segment stays a placeholder (normalizes to catalog '*') and 4xx's. Tolerant [200,400,403,404]; the GET is CALLED so the endpoint is statically reachable.
